items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1969-06-17
items.q: I had a fella called Henry Harden. He played tenor. We had two alto and tenor, you see, in the band

ctx.x: So you've been, Charlie said you've been all the way through it. That's about as hard a trumpet method you're going to find.

That was hard one too. That was hard one. Yeah. So Millie man, Millie. I tell you about Millie. Millie was a nice trumpet. That was a trumpet. That was a trumpet. Miller was a nice trouble man, he was a really nice trouble. Man, he was kind and everything, but the only thing we had trouble with Miller, man, you see that you hired Miller to play a job, man, he, nah alright, you don't told him he was going to play, said he was going to play tonight. You know what Miller do? He said, Miller be coming to the job and…

You see Edmund Warden, he used to play clarinet too. You know, he quit playing clarinet and took up the saxophone. But he had to start back on the clarinet again. Yeah, Steve was the last clarinet player. I don't know. The last one. Why do you prefer saxophone in your band? I mean why do you? Well I tell you.

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1959-11-08
items.q: I even had this fella boy, Henry Harden, playing saxophone with us too.

ctx.x: Most people don't say those things.

No, they ain't got nothing. I'm the only one got them pictures. So, alright. Like, you take like the uniforms. We used to wear a uniform, we had a jacket, a blue jacket, with a dark lapel, you know what I mean? And, blue pants with stripes. And, you know what I mean? None of them fellas don't have the jacket and the pants. I'm still got them. You stayed here? And that been years ago. I even got them white pants we used to wear. Even got that. See? You know what? Sometimes boys see me, we say, man, what? See, they…
Where you live in? He lives out on, oh near Roman Street.
